summary: Reviewed all 30 B09 case rows and resolved all 99 citations to 83 distinct test titles. Found three blocking financial defects and two major defects or evidence gaps. Provider fakes and later-package responsibilities are generally disclosed correctly. However, briefs.md and verify.log are absent; authority was recovered from the vendored registry using tools/package-brief.mjs. Agreement below concerns coverage and classification, not confirmation that tests passed.
verify_observed: verify.log is missing from the prepared workspace. Exit code, executed test counts, failures and skips are therefore unknown. No build, database or test suite was started. Read-only execution of the existing observation planner reproduced the four implementation defects below; those probes do not establish PostgreSQL test results.

findings.title: Same-amount matching can attach an unrelated provider refund to a local attempt
findings.detail: refundFor identifies an otherwise unknown provider refund solely by capture, amount and there being one local refund in flight. Neither webhook nor order-query observations prove that this provider refund belongs to that attempt. The code consequently confirms the local attempt and completes its refund using the unrelated provider identity. When the actual dispatch response subsequently carries a different refund ID, lines 1299–1301 return NO_CHANGE without recording the additional return or an UNKNOWN_REFUND incident. A read-only planner probe reproduced both transitions.
findings.reproduction: Capture 97125 cents and approve a local 1000-cent refund. Have a separate 1000-cent provider refund on the same capture whose webhook is delayed. Execute the local refund and pause CMD033 at AFTER_CALL, before settlement. Deliver the separate refund's webhook. The local refund becomes COMPLETED with the separate provider ID. Resume settlement with the actual local request's different provider refund ID: it is ignored. The provider returned 2000 cents, while the local refund facts and financial events account for only 1000. Require request-identity evidence rather than amount-based attribution.

findings.title: A reversal observed before its completed refund double-counts returned money
findings.detail: The reversal subtracts only refunds already locally COMPLETED when its event is published. observation.ts processes captures before refunds at lines 808–820 and ranks CAPTURE_ADVANCE before REFUND_TRANSITION. A newly observed refund completion therefore does not reduce the reversal. commerce-refunds.ts lines 373–385 subsequently publishes the full refund using a movable balance that also ignores reversal. FINANCE posts both returns without correction. The cited balance test covers refunds completed before reversal, not this order. The planner probe emitted a 97125-cent reversal plus a 1000-cent refund for one 97125-cent capture.
findings.reproduction: Start with a COMPLETED 97125-cent capture, no fee, UNKNOWN funds and a SUBMITTING 1000-cent refund whose successful provider response was lost. At the provider, complete that refund and reverse the remaining 96125 cents. Reconcile a snapshot containing the REVERSED capture and COMPLETED refund. The implementation publishes return events totaling 98125 cents; after the original capture posting, PSP_RECEIVABLE is -1000 instead of zero. Delivering the reversal webhook before the delayed refund observation has the same problem. Reconciliation must account for delayed refund facts without returning the same components twice.

findings.title: An earlier refund prevents the watchdog from resolving a later no-effect attempt
findings.detail: The absence check skips an in-flight refund whenever any observed refund has the same providerCaptureId, even when that observation belongs to a different, already completed local refund. apps/api/src/payments/service-commands.ts watchAttempt obtains an order-level query, so repeated watchdog/sweep reconciliation cannot prove the later attempt had no effect. It remains SUBMITTING or UNCERTAIN and continues reserving refundable balance. A read-only planner probe produced only the previous refund's DUPLICATE observation and no transition for the expired attempt.
findings.reproduction: Complete refund R1 on a capture. Approve R2 on that capture and make its dispatch time out without applying, or crash after claim before dispatch. After its deadline, return an authoritative order observation with absenceIsProof=true containing R1 only. Run watchAttempt repeatedly: line 825 treats R1's capture identity as evidence for R2 and never performs provedNoEffect for R2. Reconcile refund attempts by their request/refund identity; a prior refund on the same capture must not suppress absence proof.

findings.title: Provider fees learned with or after reversal are silently discarded
findings.detail: Fee learning runs only while the resulting capture status is COMPLETED. advanceCapture also copies a newly observed fee only when advancing to COMPLETED, at line 1041. Consequently, a previously completed capture with an unknown fee loses a fee supplied with its REVERSED observation; subsequent reversed observations still cannot record it. No fee event or inconsistency incident is produced. Read-only probes reproduced both the completion-to-reversal and already-reversed cases. This is B09's provider-fact ingestion path, not the deferred B15 bank-statement comparison.
findings.reproduction: Record a 97125-cent COMPLETED capture with providerFeeCents absent. Reconcile a REVERSED observation reporting feeCents=5275, or first reverse it and then report that fee. The planner emits no fee update or capture.fee_observed event. The ledger returns the entire capture and records zero processor expense instead of preserving the provider's retained 5275-cent fee. Repeating the query remains a duplicate. Preserve late fee facts across terminal reversal and post them using the correct post-return balance.

findings.title: Three advertised foreign-tenant denial checks use no foreign-tenant resource
findings.detail: The CMD032 DENY test advertises a refund outside the tenant/grant scope, but submits a fresh nonexistent ID and the current sale's capture ID. CMD033's corresponding loop at apps/api/test/cmd033-execute-refund.test.ts:95 uses an order ID and a nonexistent ID; CMD034 at apps/api/test/cmd034-reconcile-payment.test.ts:95 uses a quote ID and a nonexistent ID. These demonstrate missing-resource/type lookup, not isolation of an existing operation belonging to another tenant. The case map nevertheless claims every denial clause demonstrated, including EXECUTED_LOCAL for CMD032-DENY. This is an evidence defect, not proof of a tenant-access vulnerability.
findings.reproduction: Read the three denial loops and trace their IDs: none creates or addresses an existing foreign-tenant refund/order under a conflicting scope. These assertions would still return NOT_FOUND if tenant isolation were broken but nonexistent-resource lookup remained intact. Add an actual cross-scope negative control appropriate to the global operator/service roles, or explicitly leave that clause unproven instead of labeling these checks foreign-tenant evidence.
